propertyTaxRate.note: Tax Foundation Table 2 'Property Taxes Paid as a Percentage of Owner-Occupied Housing Value, 2024' (Census ACS 2024 5-year estimates): NJ 1.88% (2023: 1.98%). File value 2.23% is 0.35 pp high; it matches the Tax Foundation 2021-data figure. NJ still ranks first nationally.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans' Full Property Tax Exemption

type.quote: are granted a full property tax exemption on their dwelling house and the lot on which it is situated.

ratingRequired.quote: Active Duty Military Service, Honorable Discharge, and VA Certification of 100% permanent & total disability are still required.

ptRequired.quote: Service-connected disability declared to be a total or 100% permanent disability

requiresSchedular100.quote: Service-connected disability rated unemployable with payment of 100% and stated to be totally and permanently disabling.

wartimeRequired.quote: After December 3, 2020 wartime service is not required.

survivingSpouse.quote: Surviving spouse/civil union or domestic partner of honorably discharged 100% permanently and totally disabled veteran with active duty service

programs.note: Row is correct. TDIU rated permanent qualifies (form checkbox C). Filed any time during the tax year, prorated from date of title. Pending but NOT enacted as of 10/21/26: A1118 and A637 (2026-27) would add a proportional exemption for veterans rated below 100%; SCR84 would require State reimbursement to municipalities. None changes TY2026 or TY2027 law.

programs.name: Veteran Deduction

exemptionValue.quote: no longer need to serve during a specific war period or other emergency to receive the annual $250 property tax deduction.

survivingSpouse.quote: Surviving spouse/civil union or domestic partner of honorably discharged veteran with active duty service in the United States Armed Forces; and I have not remarried

wartimeRequired.quote: Constitutional Amendment, effective December 4, 2020, to eliminate the wartime service requirement for both the $250 Veteran Property Tax Deduction and the Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption.

type.quote: Two hundred fifty dollars ($250) may be deducted each year from taxes due on the real or personal property of qualified active duty veterans or their un-remarried surviving spouse.

programs.effectiveChanges: None enacted. ACR129 (2026-27, introduced) would raise the deduction from $250 to $2,500 over four years but requires voter approval of a constitutional amendment; not on the Nov 2026 ballot per sources found.
programs.note: The $250 is a deduction from the tax bill, not from assessed value, so `type` should be `credit` (exemptionValue 250 = dollars of tax). Surviving spouse eligibility is explicit on Form V.S.S. box B and C; the row's own details text already says so. Deceased veteran must have been a NJ resident at death.

programs.name: Active Service Deferment

survivingSpouse.quote: An active serviceperson who is deployed or mobilized for active service in time of war, may qualify for a deferment of a property tax bill.

exemptionValue.quote: Once your deployment/mobilization is over, you have 90 days to pay your deferred property taxes

programs.note: Not a rated veteran's benefit and has no dollar value (it is a deferral with interest assessed back to the due date). It should not be credited to a rated veteran's home in any dollar model; keep as informational only or set a flag so it never scores.

summary: All three NJ rows are still law; the only field errors are the $250 deduction's survivingSpouse (should be true) and its type (a bill credit, not an assessed-value reduction), and the deferment row should never be scored as a rated veteran's dollar benefit. The effective tax rate is stale: Tax Foundation 2024 data puts NJ at 1.88%, not 2.23%.
